cleanIntro: The 856 Defender is the 3-inch, six-shot .38 Special on Taurus's small frame, and Taurus's 856 book covers it - the book's own specification table gives barrel length as 2 inches or 3 inches, and its weight row calls the 3-inch figures out by name. What the book does not print is the word Defender, because Defender is the configuration, not the mechanism. The mechanism is the 856's: swing-out cylinder, six chambers, thumb piece forward, and no disassembly published at all.

steps.title: The book covers your 3-inch gun, and says so in its own table
steps.action: Read the SPECIFICATIONS table before anything else. The Barrel Length cell reads 2" or 3", and the Weight row gives separate figures for the 3-inch guns - 24 oz. for the steel and 17.5 oz. for the ultralight. That is the book stating that a 3-inch 856 is one of the guns it is written for.
steps.prose: This matters because the model name on your revolver is not in the book. Taurus indexes the 856 by four SKUs - 856, 856UL, 856CH and 856CHUL - and lets the barrel length be a variant within them rather than a separate book. Find your weight and barrel length in that table and you have found your gun.
steps.aside: Which of the four you have matters more than the barrel length: 856 and 856UL are DA/SA with an exposed hammer, 856CH and 856CHUL are concealed-hammer and double action only.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Specifications, printed p.13 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Thumb piece FORWARD, cylinder out, six chambers looked at
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece on the left side of the frame FORWARD with your right thumb, press the cylinder out to the left, and visually check that all six chambers are empty.
steps.prose: Forward is the whole trick, and it is where owners coming off other makes come unstuck - pressing the thumb piece down or inward pins the cylinder shut and the gun feels seized. Once the cylinder is out, keep it out: that swung-out position is the working state for everything that follows and it is the only access an 856 gives you.
steps.quote:
Revolver Be sure the firearm is completely unloaded and contains no cartridges or cartridge cases. With 
the thumb of the right hand push the thumb piece forward. Then press on the cylinder to swing it to the left. 
Visually check that all six (6) chambers are empty.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Firearms Safety Systems, printed p.9 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Muzzle up, one sharp push - and the longer rod is the Defender's advantage
steps.action: With the cylinder fully out, raise the muzzle and press sharply on the extractor rod. All six cases lift together on the star. Confirm every one has gone.
steps.prose: The 3-inch barrel buys you a longer ejector rod, and on a six-shot .38 that is the difference between cases dropping clear and cases standing half out to be picked. Use it - one decisive stroke with the muzzle up. It is still possible to leave a case behind if you push tentatively and let the star return under a half-lifted rim.
steps.quote:
Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. Be sure that all fired cartridges are 
ejected. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded (Fig.3).
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: Six chambers - and on a CH there is no single action to fall back on
steps.action: Confirm the count and the action: the 856 revolvers have a swing-out cylinder with six chambers turning around a central axis. On the 856 and 856UL you can cock the hammer; on the CH models the gun is double action only.
steps.prose: If your Defender is a concealed-hammer gun, every single-action instruction in the wider Taurus catalog is inapplicable to it, and the end-of-clean function check changes shape: the only way to verify the cylinder indexes and locks is a slow, full double-action stroke on an empty gun.
steps.quote:
The Taurus 856 revolvers have a swing out type cylinder with six (6) chambers, turning around a central 
axis which allows you to fire six shots.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Operating Instructions, printed p.21 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Look AND feel every chamber before solvent comes out
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into AND feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: A fingertip finds what bench light hides. A brass case head sitting deep in a .38 chamber reads as chamber wall to the eye at the wrong angle. From here the cylinder stays out; nothing else on this revolver opens.
steps.quote:
Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, 
(3) depress the thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely 
unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: The 856 is one of the few Taurus revolvers rated for +P
steps.action: If you shoot +P .38 Special through this gun, note that the Model 856 in 38 Special is named on Taurus's +P list by model. Taurus is equally clear that firing +P in a Taurus product that is NOT on that list may be dangerous.
steps.prose: Being on the list is permission, not advice - the same page says +P generates pressures well above standard and that unless you need it you should not use it, particularly for practice. For cleaning it has a practical consequence: a diet of +P puts more carbon on the cylinder face and more flame cutting at the topstrap, so check both every time.
steps.quote:
Firing +P ammunition in other Taurus products may be dangerous and can result in serious 
bodily injury or death.
Model 85 small-frame revolver in 38 Special. 
Model 856 revolvers in 38 Special.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Ammunition, printed p.19 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Every 200 rounds, and check the screws while you are in there
steps.action: Clean and lubricate at least every 200 rounds and check for loose screws or pins at the same time - tighten screws and press pins back in as needed.
steps.prose: Two hundred rounds is a light session with a six-shooter. The screws worth your attention on an 856 are the sideplate screw, the yoke screw and the grip screw; the grip screw in particular walks on the alloy-framed guns, and a loose grip on a carry revolver is felt as a shifting point of impact long before it is noticed as a maintenance item.
steps.quote:
The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps. For 
Optimal performance, we recommend you clean and lubricate your firearm for at least every 200 rounds 
fired through the firearm for optimal performance. At the same time check for any lose screws or pins. 
Tighten the screws and press pins back in as needed.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: An 856 is not every small revolver that looks like one
steps.action: Do not carry this procedure onto another snub-nosed .38 because it is the same shape. Taurus's own warning is that look-alike firearms differ in the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: The forward-sliding thumb piece is the obvious example - most other makes' cylinder latches push rearward or inward. If pushing the latch toward the muzzle does nothing, stop rather than pushing harder: you are holding a different gun.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Ammunition, printed p.19 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Field strip complete - the 856 does not come apart
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, six chambers confirmed empty, and that is the entire strip. Taurus publishes no disassembly for the 856 and states the revolver is cleaned and lubricated without any disassembly steps, so the sideplate stays on and the yoke stays in.
steps.prose: The part list in the back runs from the cylinder assembly through the transfer bar to the sideplate screw and comes with no order of operations - it is a list for ordering, not an invitation. If an 856 needs to be opened, the book's route is a qualified gunsmith or Taurus Customer Care.
steps.quote: The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without any disassembly steps.
steps.cite:
856/856UL
856CH/856CHUL
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 5 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.23 (PDF p.12)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus 856 book publishes no disassembly at all. It states that the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions WITHOUT any disassembly steps, asks for a clean every 200 rounds with a check for loose screws and pins, and gives a four-item routine. The exploded view and part list at the back are for ordering parts and carry no sequence; the book routes malfunctions and repairs to a qualified gunsmith or Taurus Customer Care. Nothing deeper is published, so nothing deeper is walked - and the 3-inch barrel changes none of that.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chambers with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent, then run a dry cotton patch through
Do all six chambers, not just the bore - a .38 chamber that has carried lead loads builds a ring at the case mouth that makes extraction sticky
A 3-inch barrel gives you more rifling than the snub does; work the forcing cone just ahead of the gap hardest
Hold the barrel to a light and confirm a clear bore before the revolver is put away

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACE, STAR & FRAME WINDOW
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and clear residue from small crevices with a small brush
Work the carbon ring off the FRONT face of the cylinder - it is the deposit that eventually stops the cylinder closing
Push the extractor rod back and clean behind the star; grit under the star is what makes a cylinder refuse to index
Wipe the barrel/cylinder gap area, the forcing cone and the topstrap above it, and look for flame cutting on a gun fed +P

cleaning.name: OIL, SCREWS & STORAGE
tasks: After cleaning, rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth for a thin protective film
A drop of oil at the crane and on the moving parts - a drop, not a flood, which only migrates into the lockwork
Check the sideplate, yoke and grip screws are tight and press any proud pins back in
A revolver fitted with a laser must not be cleaned in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it

reassembly: Nothing came off, so nothing goes back on. Let the extractor rod re-seat fully before the cylinder goes home.
Close the cylinder gently but firmly until it latches - never flick it open or snap it shut, which knocks the crane out of true.
Rotate the closed cylinder by hand and feel it index and lock into each of the six notches before the revolver is stored.
fncheck: With all six chambers confirmed empty: the cylinder should latch with light thumb pressure and show no perceptible side play; hand-rotating it should feel the cylinder stop drop into each notch; on a DA/SA 856 the hammer should hold at full cock and the transfer bar should rise only as the trigger goes fully through, and on an 856CH the same is checked by riding the double-action stroke slowly. Both actions must reset positively when the trigger returns all the way forward.
